key_insight: Failures that threaten safety can be rare, complex, or adversarially hidden and only become apparent when multiple agent traces are analyzed jointly; this paper shows that searching and judging traces at the set level—rather than individually—substantially improves detection of such violations.
problem_solved: Auditors struggle to find rare, multi-trace, or covert safety violations (e.g., misuse campaigns, covert sabotage, reward hacking, prompt injection) when evaluating traces independently; the work addresses the need to detect failures that only emerge from relationships across many traces.
method: Formulate detection as a search over large collections of agent traces and apply joint/set-level evaluation rather than per-trace judgments.
Use aggregation and cross-trace analysis techniques to surface patterns and interactions that reveal hidden or rare failures.
Design detection procedures robust to adversarial hiding—prioritizing trace subsets for inspection and amplifying signals that only appear in combination.
impact: Enables more reliable, scalable safety audits by making rare, coordinated, or adversarially concealed failures discoverable; helps practitioners prioritize inspections and reduce undetected risk in deployed agents.
visual_elements: Schematic showing many agent traces as parallel timelines with a rare failure highlighted only after overlapping multiple traces are combined.
Flowchart of the joint-analysis pipeline: collect traces → group/score trace sets → prioritize subsets → human or automated review.
Bar/line chart comparing detection rates of per-trace judges vs. multi-trace/joint detectors across varying failure rarity.
Icon set: magnifying glass over a network of traces, shield (safety), and warning symbol for detected violations.
paper_title: Detecting Safety Violations Across Many Agent Traces
paper_authors: Adam Stein, Davis Brown, Hamed Hassani, Mayur Naik, Eric Wong
